text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Three elderly citizens were convicted of genocide against the Lithuanian nation for taking part in the murder of a family who were hiding from the Soviet secret police in 1945.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius met a visiting IMF mission on Tuesday and said he wanted to reach a compromise with the Fund to allow Lithuania to keep import tariffs higher for longer.
- Share prices have begun to fall on the bourse.
- Parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis is on a visit to Tallinn and urged the three Baltic states to cooperate.

- Justice Minister Vytautas Pakalniskis said that the prosecutor's office should be brought under the administration of the justice ministry. It is currently independent from all ministries. The office was at the centre of controversy earlier this week when the prosecutor general resigned, saying he could not cope with the rising crime situation.
